claim: Resistance holds us back from acting, from being the man we want to be and know we can be
Resistance shows up in lots of forms, but at the real root of it, resistance is fear: we fear, so we don't act
In a lot of cases we fear the unknown
Changing our diet or body, building that business or relationship: mostly we fear change because it's unknown, and that stops us from taking action so often

So much of what is coached and suggested on this podcast is about moving past fear to take action: not the individual technique, but fundamentally shifting your relationship with fear and resistance inside you
Everything in our lives is an inside game

Being the man you want to be has nothing to do with the outside world and everything to do with what's inside you, which determines your actions, how your relationship goes, how you take care of your body
The number one thing that keeps you from going where you want and living the day-to-day you want is fear and resistance
One huge concern right now, in the pandemic: so many people are getting in a state of fear, and their resistance is getting so much stronger
The world situation has maybe accelerated people's fear and resistance, made it more pronounced: the world wants you held back, literally saying stay at home, and wants you afraid
We've gotta fight the fear and resistance the world wants, and it's about the day-to-day actions
Doing the work every single day is not about looks: no measuring biceps on social media

claim: Do the work physically and you'll feel such a difference in how willing you are to step into the unknown
The unknown is discomfort, and we fear both
A lot of times fearing the unknown and discomfort is why we don't push harder when we train: mostly not because we can't, but because we fear the discomfort, not knowing what we can or can't do
The more often we push into the unknown space, the more comfortable we get with it, and it carries through to everything
The more often you step into a cold shower, the more you convince yourself: "I can step into the unknown. I can step into discomfort"
Do the daily work not for your looks or weight, but because the fear and resistance inside you is there and is not going anywhere
The best way to kick the ass of the fear and resistance inside you is the little things every single day, each a little jab right to its face

claim: Across the five pillars of power, fitness, nutrition, hormones, sex and mind, plugging where we leak power and building it adds up to completely shifting our relationship with fear and resistance

Besides better shape and feeling better, most importantly, plugging where you leak power and building it across the five pillars makes you willing to step into discomfort and the unknown: you fear less, act more, are more confident, and when those change, everything changes
There's a compound effect to plugging where you leak power and building it across the five pillars: every day in that new position you feel the change more

Doing the work across the five pillars, you'll see some changes in 30 days, and can see dramatic changes in a short period of time, but applied for six months, a year, two years, "What I can tell you happens is dramatic, complete changes" toward the real, powerful version of you
We do the work every day because of the compound effect: it adds up
A lot of guys are doing the work, seen in Bootcamp and among guys talked to

Doing the work is not just physical training: it also means being willing to face and process your emotions, to meditate and find the quiet space within you, to have the conversations in your relationship, to eat clean

claim: Do the work in the little moments: the choice of what to eat or buy, the moment you decide to get moving, to start the conversation, to sit down to meditate

Whether you meditate 10 minutes, 20 or five, the part that matters by far the most, "like a thousand times more than all the rest of it", is the two or five seconds when you sit down and hit play: with Headspace, for example, pull it up, hit play, set your phone aside
The five seconds when you sit down to meditate and hit play are a huge determining factor in your life
The choice at the store is very, very brief, but it ripples out to all the rest of the moments in your life
You know the little moments: do the work in them, and it adds up
